speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when the fever and seizure started, and did the rash appear before or after the seizure?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the fever resolve before the rash appeared, and have you noticed any swelling of the lymph nodes behind the ears or at the back of the neck? Also, are there any red spots around the mouth or eyes?

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash appearing after the fever resolved is a classic sign of roseola infantum, typically caused by HHV-6. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other causes, I will check for specific lymph node involvement. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: Within normal limits for age

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CBC and classic presentation of high fever followed by a rash as the fever breaks strongly support a diagnosis of roseola infantum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola infantum
